messages:
marta: Starting onboarding for RareBird-3B-v1 pulled from FeatherAI's hub. Customer wants an air-gapped container with quantized weights for on-prem.
pranav: Which license? Can you paste the relevant parts?
marta: Pasted license snippet:
```
FeatherAI Model License v1.0
Section 2: Non-commercial use only
Section 4: Redistribution of weights prohibited without express written consent; derivative quantized binaries treated as \"derivative works\"
Section 7: Attribution required: include authors and link to model card
```
lisa (Legal): Quick read: NC + explicit redistribution ban. Immediate takeaways:
- We cannot ship quantized weights to a paying customer without an explicit commercial sublicense from FeatherAI.
- Hosting (hosted API or Private managed in-customer VPC) is usually OK provided we do not hand over the weights.
- Quantized derivatives are likely covered by the redistribution language.
tyler: Infra note: we can deliver Redwood Private (managed appliance or VPC) so the customer runs inference without receiving weights, which avoids redistribution.
marta: But customer insists on an air-gapped self-run container they can keep on-prem with no network connectivity. They'll push back if we refuse.
pranav: Options we should consider:
1) Request a commercial redistribution sublicense from FeatherAI (written, may include fees/terms).
2) Offer managed Private as an interim so they can run without receiving weights.
3) BYOW (bring-your-own-weights) flow: we provide the runtime/container and docs; customer supplies the weights and proof of license. This needs strict attestation and verification.
lisa (Legal): Option 3 can work only if Redwood never possesses or distributes the weights. We need customer attestation, checksum verification, and contractual indemnity for licensing violations. Legal/BD must handle any sublicensing negotiation — we should not act as the intermediary for licensing terms unless approved.
pranav: For BYOW we need an onboarding checklist: customer license attestation, upload checksum verification, contract clause transferring liability/indemnity.
tyler: Operational constraints: our packaging currently includes AUTHORS and LICENSE files in runtime bundles. For a BYOW installer, require customers to mount weights at a local path that our runtime reads but doesn't upload or persist. Add CI hooks to confirm no S3 persistence.
marta: ML eval note: Our 4-bit quantization experiments show ~8% throughput gain but a small drop in summarization BLEU (~0.7 absolute). If we distribute quantized weights, does that change attribution or redistribution obligations?
lisa (Legal): Attribution requirements apply regardless of hosting vs distribution — include authors and model card link in UI and docs. But handing over a quantized checkpoint is redistribution under Section 4; metadata files alone don't avoid that. Get explicit written permission.
pranav: Draft message to FeatherAI (suggested):
"Hi FeatherAI — we're evaluating RareBird-3B-v1 for an enterprise on-prem deployment. Do you offer a commercial redistribution sublicense for quantized/derivative weights? If not, can you confirm whether managed hosting or a BYOW approach is acceptable under your TOS? Please advise contact for licensing. —Pranav, Redwood"
marta: I'll send that now and flag this as blocked for an on-prem deliverable until we receive a commercial sublicense or other written permission.
ops-bot: deploy-notify: new-private-offer-template v0.9 pushed to /infra/packaging (link)
pranav: Opening eval ticket EVAL-4237 to investigate the 4-bit quality regressions and across our summarization suites.
tyler: I'll draft a BYOW runtime blueprint with the following: local-only weight mount, checksum verification, no upload enforced by runtime, bundled AUTHORS + attribution docs, and automated audit checks.
marta: Thanks. Keep Legal CC'd on any replies from FeatherAI and request the exact sublicense wording and any verbatim attribution text they require.
lisa (Legal): Agreed. Also capture any sample commercial sublicense text so BD can evaluate pricing/terms.
marta: Ack — I'll post updates once FeatherAI replies. Blocking on written permission for on-prem container delivery.
